title.datacite:title: Virtual English LAB: The Impact of Virtual Worlds on English Language Learning and Life Skills in Higher Education

descriptions.value: This study investigates the impact of immersive three-dimensional virtual environments on language learning and professional skills development in Higher Education. Grounded in constructivist and socio-cultural pedagogies, the research explores the implementation of the English LAB Virtual World – FrameVR-based educational platform – within two university-level English language laboratory courses for future primary school teachers. Adopting a quasi-experimental, mixed-methods design, the study analyzes learning outcomes, motivation, life skills, and perceived usability through validated tools: Cambridge Assessment-aligned tests (A2/B1), the MSLQ, the LiSST scale, and the SUS questionnaire. The experimental group, engaged in blended learning within the immersive environment, demonstrated statistically significant improvements in grammar, vocabulary, listening, and speaking skills (p < 0.001), alongside enhanced intrinsic motivation and substantial growth in life skills domains such as critical thinking, collaboration, and self-efficacy. Correlational analyses revealed strong associations between perceived usability, motivation, and transversal skills development. Qualitative data from focus groups further confirmed the transformative nature of immersive learning, emphasizing engagement, agency, and collaborative dynamics. The findings support the potential of Virtual Worlds to function not only as linguistic learning platforms but also as pedagogical ecosystems for developing 21st-century competencies. This research contributes to the evolving paradigm of the Eduverse, suggesting that virtual environments – when purposefully designed and pedagogically structured –can act as strategic enablers of inclusive, student-centered, and transformative learning in Higher Education.

DC.Description.content: This study investigates the impact of immersive three-dimensional virtual environments on language learning and professional skills development in Higher Education. Grounded in constructivist and socio-cultural pedagogies, the research explores the implementation of the English LAB Virtual World – FrameVR-based educational platform – within two university-level English language laboratory courses for future primary school teachers. Adopting a quasi-experimental, mixed-methods design, the study analyzes learning outcomes, motivation, life skills, and perceived usability through validated tools: Cambridge Assessment-aligned tests (A2/B1), the MSLQ, the LiSST scale, and the SUS questionnaire. The experimental group, engaged in blended learning within the immersive environment, demonstrated statistically significant improvements in grammar, vocabulary, listening, and speaking skills (p < 0.001), alongside enhanced intrinsic motivation and substantial growth in life skills domains such as critical thinking, collaboration, and self-efficacy. Correlational analyses revealed strong associations between perceived usability, motivation, and transversal skills development. Qualitative data from focus groups further confirmed the transformative nature of immersive learning, emphasizing engagement, agency, and collaborative dynamics. The findings support the potential of Virtual Worlds to function not only as linguistic learning platforms but also as pedagogical ecosystems for developing 21st-century competencies. This research contributes to the evolving paradigm of the Eduverse, suggesting that virtual environments – when purposefully designed and pedagogically structured –can act as strategic enablers of inclusive, student-centered, and transformative learning in Higher Education.

def _extract_openaire_and_internal_dates(self, file_bundle: Dict[str, Any], interactive_resolution: bool = False, ai_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        citation_date = iso_date(self.meta.first("citation_date"))
        dc_created = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.created"))
        dc_submitted = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.dateSubmitted"))
        dc_issued = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.issued"))
        dc_modified = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.modified"))
        dc_accepted = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.accepted"))
        dc_available = iso_date(self.meta.first("DC.Date.available"))
        dom_submitted = iso_date(self._dd_value_after_dt("Inviata"))
        dom_published = iso_date(self._dd_value_after_dt("Pubblicato"))
        pdf_dates = self._extract_pdf_editorial_dates(file_bundle)
        page_rights = self._extract_page_rights_holder_and_year()

        def choose_published_date(citation_date, dom_published, dc_created, dc_issued, dc_modified):
            return citation_date or dom_published or dc_created or dc_issued or dc_modified

        page_candidates = {
            "title": self.meta.first("citation_title") or self.meta.first("DC.Title") or self._text("h1.article-page__title span"),
            "submitted_date": dc_submitted or dom_submitted,
            "accepted_date": dc_accepted,
            "copyright_holder": page_rights.get("copyright_holder_page"),
            "copyright_year": str(page_rights.get("copyright_year_page")) if page_rights.get("copyright_year_page") is not None else None,
            "license_url": self._extract_access_rights_and_license().get("licenseCondition", {}).get("uri"),
        }
        pdf_ai_diag = self._request_ai_pdf_front_analysis(pdf_dates, page_candidates, ai_config)
        pdf_ai_result = pdf_ai_diag.get("result") if isinstance(pdf_ai_diag, dict) and pdf_ai_diag.get("status") == "ok" else {}
        pdf_fields = pdf_ai_result.get("pdf_fields", {}) if isinstance(pdf_ai_result, dict) else {}
        ai_resolution = pdf_ai_result.get("resolution", {}) if isinstance(pdf_ai_result, dict) else {}

        pdf_submitted_value = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("submitted_date") or {}).get("value")) or pdf_dates.get("submitted_pdf")
        pdf_accepted_value = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("accepted_date") or {}).get("value")) or pdf_dates.get("accepted_pdf")
        pdf_copyright_holder = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("copyright_holder") or {}).get("value")) or pdf_dates.get("copyright_holder_pdf")
        pdf_copyright_year = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("copyright_year") or {}).get("value")) or (str(pdf_dates.get("copyright_year_pdf")) if pdf_dates.get("copyright_year_pdf") is not None else None)
        pdf_title_value = normalize_space((pdf_fields.get("title") or {}).get("value"))
        pdf_title_allowed = bool((pdf_fields.get("title") or {}).get("use_allowed")) if isinstance(pdf_fields.get("title"), dict) else False

        strong_page_published = citation_date or dom_published or dc_created
        if strong_page_published and dc_issued and strong_page_published != dc_issued:
            self._warn(
                code="PUBLISHED_DATE_CONFLICT",
                message=f"Published-date conflict: stronger page signal '{strong_page_published}' overrides DC.Date.issued '{dc_issued}'.",
                function_name="_extract_openaire_and_internal_dates",
                context={
                    "citation_date": citation_date,
                    "dom_published": dom_published,
                    "dc_created": dc_created,
                    "dc_issued": dc_issued,
                    "dc_modified": dc_modified,
                },
            )

        issued = choose_published_date(
            citation_date,
            dom_published,
            dc_created,
            dc_issued,
            dc_modified,
        )
        available = dc_available or issued
        submitted_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy("submitted_date", dc_submitted or dom_submitted, pdf_submitted_value, interactive_resolution, prefer="pdf", ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("submitted_date") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None)
        accepted_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy("accepted_date", dc_accepted, pdf_accepted_value, interactive_resolution, prefer="pdf", ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("accepted_date") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None)
        copyright_holder_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy("copyright_holder", page_rights.get("copyright_holder_page"), pdf_copyright_holder, interactive_resolution, prefer="pdf", ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("copyright_holder") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None)
        copyright_year_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy(
            "copyright_year",
            str(page_rights.get("copyright_year_page")) if page_rights.get("copyright_year_page") is not None else None,
            pdf_copyright_year,
            interactive_resolution,
            prefer="pdf",
            ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("copyright_year") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None,
        )
        title_resolution = self._resolve_discrepancy(
            "title",
            page_candidates.get("title"),
            pdf_title_value if pdf_title_allowed or not page_candidates.get("title") else None,
            interactive_resolution,
            prefer="page",
            ai_resolution=ai_resolution.get("title") if isinstance(ai_resolution, dict) else None,
        )

        accepted = accepted_resolution.get("chosen_value")
        submitted = submitted_resolution.get("chosen_value")

        export_dates: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        if accepted:
            export_dates.append({"value": accepted, "dateType": "Accepted", "source": accepted_resolution.get("chosen_source")})
        if available:
            export_dates.append({"value": available, "dateType": "Available", "source": "meta:DC.Date.available" if dc_available else "fallback:Issued"})
        if issued:
            export_dates.append({"value": issued, "dateType": "Issued", "source": "meta:DC.Date.issued" if dc_issued else "meta:citation_date" if citation_date else "dom:Pubblicato" if dom_published else "meta:DC.Date.created"})

        export_dates = dedupe_list(export_dates)
        dates_by_type: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {d["dateType"]: d["value"] for d in export_dates}
        if not dates_by_type.get("Available") and issued:
            dates_by_type["Available"] = issued
        internal_dates = {
            "submitted": submitted,
            "accepted": accepted,
            "created": dc_created,
            "modified": dc_modified,
            "issued": issued,
            "available": dates_by_type.get("Available"),
            "submitted_page": dc_submitted or dom_submitted,
            "submitted_pdf": pdf_dates.get("submitted_pdf"),
            "accepted_page": dc_accepted,
            "accepted_pdf": pdf_dates.get("accepted_pdf"),
        }
        resolutions = {
            "title": title_resolution,
            "submitted": submitted_resolution,
            "accepted": accepted_resolution,
            "copyright_holder": copyright_holder_resolution,
            "copyright_year": copyright_year_resolution,
        }
        return {
            "export_dates": export_dates,
            "dates_by_type": dates_by_type,
            "internal_dates": internal_dates,
            "pdf_editorial_dates": pdf_dates,
            "page_rights": page_rights,
            "resolutions": resolutions,
            "pdf_ai_resolution": pdf_ai_diag,
        }

This work is therefore part of the research aimed at exploring the impact of the use of immersive virtual environments within Higher Education, with particular reference to the teachi ng of the English language aimed at university students training to teach in primary schools. 2. Theoretical framework of reference 2.1 Educational innovation and immersive environments in higher education Teaching innovation in the university environment can no longer ignore a radical rethinking of learning methodologies and environments. In fact, in line with the principles of the constructivist and socio-cultural approach (Vygotskij, 1978), attention has shifted from the one-way transmission of knowledge to educational models centere d on the student, on collaboration and on active learning. In a decidedly transformative perspective, immersive technologies – such as 3D virtual worlds – represent not only technical tools, but real pedagogical environments capab le of transforming the educational relationship and enabling innovative teach ing practices in a radical paradigm shift (Garrison & Akyol, 2013). Virtual Worlds are interactive and pe rsistent three-dimensional digital environments, designed to simulate real or imaginary contexts in which users, represented by avatars, can interact with each other and with virtual objects in real time. These environments are configured as immersive and participatory spaces capable of promoting experiential learning, peer collaboration and the development of transversal skills su ch as problem solving, effective communication and adaptability (Filippone et al., 2023). They are learning spaces characterized by teaching materials, interactive games to enhance learning, materials for assessing learning and metacognitive reflection, virtual places in which to meet to co-construct learning through cooperative study, simulating the school e nvironment, reachable, however, at any time of the day so as to encourag e the personal study process (Filippone et al., 2023/a).
